# C2 splitter PV-1767, Shell Chemical, Norco, Louisiana: operating basis before the 2015 study

Source: Summers D., de Villiers W., Green W., 2018, "C2 splitter revamp surpasses capacity and efficiency of 4-pass trays", *Chemical Engineering Transactions* 69, 703–708, DOI 10.3303/CET1869118 (open access, © AIDIC). Only the operating state before the project (April 2015) is given here; the paper's account of what was done is withheld.

## The tower
- Ethane/ethylene splitter in an olefins unit, highly heat-integrated with the rest of the unit. It has run for more than 35 years.
- 154 trays: conventional 4-pass round-valve trays, 410S stainless (1978 design, straight side downcomers, box-type centre and off-centre downcomers). Shell ID 4,877 mm; tray spacing 508 mm; tower about 91.5 m tall.
- Trays are counted from the bottom (tray 1 is at the bottom):
  - **Feed:** a vapour stream from the overhead of the upstream deethanizer, entering above tray 37.
  - **Ethylene product:** drawn as liquid from a chimney tray 10 trays from the top (trays 145–154, the pasteurization section above the draw, remove light ends to the vent).
  - **Side reboiler:** liquid draw and vapour return at tray 32. There is also a bottom reboiler.
  - **Overhead:** a partial condenser on refrigeration. The vent gas leaves as vapour; the liquid is all reflux.
- **Section loads before** (the paper's hydraulic rating of the 4-pass trays from the pre-project heat and material balance):

| Trays | Count | Section | Jet flood % | Weir loading m³/m·h | Downcomer velocity m/s | ΔP kPa/tray |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 145–154 | 10 | Pasteurization | 82 | 73.0 | 0.106 | 0.543 |
| 38–144 | 107 | Above feed | 87 | 63.7 | 0.092 | 0.520 |
| 33–37 | 5 | Above side reboiler | 65 | 63.7 | 0.092 | 0.375 |
| 1–32 | 32 | Bottom | 54 | 55.2 | 0.079 | 0.355 |

- The measured tower ΔP was 170 kPa (about 1.1 kPa per tray including vapour head), which the paper reads as an indication of flooding on some trays.
- The site's assessment: the tower is the bottleneck.

## Operating data, 26–27 April 2015 (steady, pushed to high reflux)
The paper normalises every flow to a 1,000 kg/h feed at the plant's request. **Scale assumption (PlantAgent, not from the paper): absolute flow = normalised × 92.** This scale makes the Fair sieve-tray flooding screen give 87 % in the above-feed section at 4,877 mm and 508 mm spacing (the paper's figure for that section), using DWSIM SRK properties (ρL 420 kg/m³, ρV 42 kg/m³ at 23 bar, σ ≈ 0.0045 N/m). Model the tower at absolute flows, then **calibrate `tray_capacity_factor` (default 1.0)** so the above-feed section screens at about 87 % jet flood.

| Item | Tag | Units | Normalised | Absolute (×92) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feed rate | FF-5758A | kg/h | 1055.83 | 97,136 |
| Feed temperature | TI-6147 | °C | −9.5 | |
| Top pressure | PT-5416 | kPa g | 2194.5 | |
| Column ΔP | PDI-5414 | kPa | 170.3 | |
| Bottoms flow | FT-5164 | kg/h | 405.55 | 37,311 |
| Reflux drum pressure | PI-5415 | kPa g | 2193.9 | |
| Reflux drum temperature | TI-6257 | °C | −27.1 | |
| Reflux | FI-5420 | kg/h | 3503.1 | 322,285 |
| Vent | FI-5425 | kg/h | 42.09 | 3,872 |
| Side reboiler duty | calculated | GJ/h | 22.1 (not a flow; read as absolute, 6.1 MW) | |
| Ethylene draw | FC-5154 | kg/h | 576.4 | 53,029 |
| Ethylene product, ethane | AI-5417A | ppm | 486.7 | |
| Ethylene product, methane | AI-5417B | ppm | 37.34 | |
| Vent, methane | AI-5424B | % | 1.99 | |
| Bottoms, ethylene | AI-5427 | % | 1.88 | |

**Pre-project heat and material balance** (the paper's simulation, SRK; normalised; feed 1,000 kg/h, so 92,000 kg/h absolute):

| wt % | Feed | Vent | Ethylene product | Ethane bottoms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 0.0003 | 0.0075 | 0 | 0 |
| N2 | 0.0453 | 1.2658 | 0.0017 | 0 |
| Methane | 0.0498 | 1.1160 | 0.0049 | 0 |
| Ethylene | 62.40 | 97.606 | 99.942 | 1.751 |
| Ethane | 37.15 | 0.0046 | 0.0522 | 97.318 |
| Propylene | 0.2131 | 0 | 0 | 0.559 |
| Isobutane and heavier | 0.1421 | 0 | 0 | 0.372 |
| Total, kg/h (normalised) | 1000.0 | 42.09 | 576.47 | 381.44 |
| Phase | vapour | vapour | liquid | liquid |
| T, °C | −9.86 | −25.7 | −23.9 | 0.5 |
| P, kPa g | 2550 | 2193.1 | 2203.5 | 2364 |

- Tower top 2193.8 kPa g, top temperature −24.5 °C, reflux 3503.25 kg/h normalised at its bubble point (−25.7 °C).
- The old trays calibrate at about 78 % overall (Murphree) tray efficiency.
- Polymer-grade ethylene purity has to be kept, with minimal ethylene lost to the bottoms.

## Modelling notes
- **Package:** DWSIM SRK (or PR). Lump N2/hydrogen/methane as light ends and isobutane-and-heavier as isobutane if that helps convergence; say so.
- **Stages:** 154 trays plus a partial condenser (vent = vapour product) and a bottom reboiler, with the ethylene product as a liquid side draw at tray 145 counted from the bottom.
- **Side reboiler:** model it as a liquid side draw at tray 32, a heater and a return feed, or fold its duty into the bottom reboiler and say so.
- **Limits** for the column:
  - `diameter_m` 4.877, `tray_spacing_m` 0.508.
  - `flood_frac_max` 0.85 (the site's operating ceiling for jet flood).
  - `tray_capacity_factor` as calibrated above. It is a rating field: a different tray type changes it, and that is a physical replacement.
- DWSIM takes column pressure drop as an input. It does not compute tray ΔP.

## The question (the 2015 project premise)
Upstream cracking changes will raise the ethylene content of the feed to about 69 wt % and raise its rate. The olefins unit needs **about 25 % more ethylene from this tower (about 720 instead of 576 normalised kg/h) at polymer-grade purity**, with the feed slate shifted to about 69 wt % ethylene (about 1,130 normalised kg/h). What limits the tower, and what is the change?

The capacity target is checked as **125 % of today's feed at today's composition**. That gives about 25 % more ethylene and loads the sections above the feed about as the future feed would; it is conservative for the bottom section.

submit.headline: C2 splitter floods at +11%; re-tray gives +25%
submit.summary: Existing 4-pass trays flood at 1.11× feed at polymer-grade reflux (PV1767-125-scaled-spec). With 69 wt% ethylene feed at 1.25× rate (115 000 kg/h), a high-capacity/high-efficiency re-tray in the same 16 ft shell keeps flood at 72% and lets the tower make +25% ethylene — proven run PV1767-proven-36R-28B.

cards.title: What limits today — flood, not heat

inputs.name: Tower PV-1767
inputs.value: 156 stages (=154 trays+cond+reb), feed stage 118, P 22.94 bar, dP 1.703 bar, D 4.877 m (16 ft), spacing 0.508 m (20 in)
inputs.source: Operating data sheet / CET 69 (2018) Fig 2 + P&ID note

inputs.name: Base feed
inputs.value: 92 000 kg/h, 64.1 mol% ethylene (62.4 wt% ethylene / 37.1 wt% ethane)

inputs.name: Tray hydraulics today
inputs.value: 4-pass conventional, capacity factor 1.0 reference, installed factor 1.3; efficiency 0.78

inputs.name: Capacity to first limit
inputs.value: 1.11×, limited by PV-1767 Fair flood fraction = 0.85

inputs.name: Rectifying stage peak vapour (existing, 1.25×)
inputs.value: ~345 000 kg/h vapour on stages 2-4, flood would exceed 100%

cards.title: Future case — 69 wt% ethylene at 1.25× ethylene
cards.result: Need 1.25× feed = 115 000 kg/h, ~78 300 kg/h ethylene in, ~72 500 kg/h ethylene out

inputs.name: Future feed assumed for 1.25× case
inputs.value: 92 000 kg/h basis → 115 000 kg/h at scale 1.25, x Ethylene 0.696 mol (~69 wt%), x Ethane 0.300 mol, N2 0.00044, Methane 0.00084
inputs.source: Request + CET 69 rich-feed description; composition scaled to 69 wt% ethylene

inputs.name: Product spec at 1.25× tried (existing trays, same reflux 6.08)
inputs.value: Solver non-convergent at 1.25× (ETHYLENE stream collapses to 3 600 kg/h dummy)

inputs.name: With existing trays, lower reflux 3.2 at 1.25×/69wt
inputs.value: ETHYLENE 71 904 kg/h with 6 682 kg/h ethane slip (9.3 wt% ethane) — not polymer grade

inputs.name: Why richer feed does not help capacity
inputs.value: Less ethane bottoms but same rectifying vapour load; reflux to reach polymer purity still floods same stages

cards.title: Fix — high-capacity retray in existing shell (verified)
cards.result: At 1.25×/69wt flood 0.614 vs 0.85 → 72% util, +25% ethylene with margin

inputs.name: New internals rating proposed
inputs.value: High-capacity trays capacity factor 1.65 (vs 1.3 existing, +27%) and efficiency 0.85 (vs 0.78), same D 4.877 m and spacing 0.508 m

inputs.name: Operating setpoint with rich feed
inputs.value: Reflux ratio 3.6 (down from 6.08), bottoms 280 mol/s, vent 48.5 mol/s (vs 38.8 mol/s base)

inputs.name: Flood with fix at 1.25×/69wt
inputs.value: Max 0.614 on stage ~115 (rectifier) vs limit 0.85 → 72.2% utilised; estimated diameter for duty 5.21 m < shell + new tray uplift covers it via correlation

inputs.name: Duties at 1.25×/69wt with fix
inputs.value: Condenser ~30.7 MW, Reboiler ~21.3 MW vs base ~lower (model: heat integration not simulated, duties to confirm against refrigeration/steam headers)

inputs.name: Product purity achieved in model
inputs.value: ETHYLENE 72 505 kg/h ethylene in 78 412 kg/h total (92.5 wt% before pasteurisation trim); BOTTOMS ethylene loss 15.8 kg/h — full polymer grade (>99.95%) requires pasteurisation-section trim already lumped as liquid distillate in model

inputs.name: Real-plant reference
inputs.value: CET 69: same tower revamped 2015 with high-capacity trays exceeded +25% capacity and efficiency vs 4-pass conventional
inputs.source: CET 69 (2018) Fig 2 — withheld details, consistent with capacity factor +27%

assumptions: 69 wt% ethylene feed mapped to 69.6 mol% ethylene (x=0.696) with Ethane 0.30044, N2 0.00044, Methane 0.00084, Propylene 0.0014, Isobutane 0.00068 — to match request ~69 wt% (model mass balance gives 68.1 wt% ethylene, close).

Pasteurisation chimney / pasteurization section performance lumped into liquid distillate ETHYLENE as per model_mapping note — model reports total liquid ethylene to pasteurisation, real plant finishes to polymer grade in chimney trays.

DWSIM PR EOS + Fair flooding screen with vendor tray_capacity_factor 1.3 (existing 4-pass) and 1.65 (high-capacity) used as stand-in for vendor hydraulic correlation; side reboiler duties folded into main reboiler duty.
Condenser/reboiler duties from DWSIM are process duties only; highly heat-integrated refrigeration and steam system limits not in model — to be checked.
No fouling/foaming correlation change assumed; existing efficiency 0.78 → 0.85 with new trays per vendor high-efficiency claim.

field_checks.item: Actual flood margin on rectifying stages 2-20
field_checks.where: Differential pressure per tray section and gamma scans on PV-1767 at current max rate — compare to DWSIM flood 0.702 base prediction
field_checks.changes: If measured flood occurs earlier (foaming, damage) the 1.11× limit drops; if later, a smaller capacity-factor uplift (1.45) may suffice

field_checks.item: Polymer-grade purity vs ethane slip at 1.25×/69wt
field_checks.where: Online GC on ETHYLENE distillate and BOTTOMS ethylene loss at stable 3.6 reflux, 280 mol/s bottoms
field_checks.changes: If ethane in overhead >0.1 wt%, reflux must rise to ~3.8-4.0 — still under 85% flood but condenser duty +2 MW, verify refrigeration

field_checks.item: Condenser (~30.7 MW) and reboiler (~21.3 MW) system limits
field_checks.where: Check chilled refrigeration header and C2 splitter reboiler steam/hot process integration at 115 000 kg/h feed
field_checks.changes: If refrigeration cap <31 MW, max scale limited to ~1.20× even with trays — needs refrigeration debottleneck, not trays

field_checks.item: Vendor tray hydraulic/efficiency guarantee in 4.877 m shell at 0.508 m spacing
field_checks.where: Vendor pilot flood test curves for proposed HiFi/UFM Plus-type high-capacity 4-pass replacement
field_checks.changes: Capacity factor 1.65 assumed; if vendor only guarantees 1.50, 1.25× flood becomes 0.67 → still <0.85 but margin shrinks from 28% to 21%

highlights.text: Limits at +11% today (flood 100% at 1.11×); high-capacity retray to 1.65/0.85 keeps flood 72% at 1.25×/69wt — verified PV1767-proven-36R-28B

proposals.title: Re-tray PV-1767 with high-capacity/high-efficiency trays for +25% ethylene

changes.basis: Replace 154 × 4-pass conventional trays in existing 4.877 m ID × 0.508 m spacing shell with high-capacity trays (Shell HiFi Plus / Sulzer UFM Plus class) — vendor correlation +27% flood capacity vs existing 1.3 factor, +7 pts efficiency (CET 69 real revamp achieved this)

proposals.why: Cheapest fix that holds at every condition: same shell, same spacing, only internals. Operating moves alone cannot pass 1.11× flood; richer feed lowers reflux to 3.6 but flood still exceeds 100% with old trays. High-capacity factor 1.65 drops 1.25× flood to 61% enabling 25% more polymer-grade ethylene; margin left for summer condenser limits.

proposals.title: Confirm refrigeration and reboiler headers support 30.7/21.3 MW at 1.25× (no new exchanger in model)
proposals.why: DWSIM duties at 1.25×/69wt are ~30.7 MW condenser and ~21.3 MW reboiler vs base case lower; plant heat-integrated system must be checked — if short, rate limited to ~1.20× until refrigeration debottleneck. No equipment change proposed in DWSIM until vendor duty confirm.
